issues.description: Mode-to-bytes dispatch is duplicated between sign_message and verify_signature, allowing signer/verifier drift.
issues.detail: Both functions in chia/wallet/util/signing.py carry the same four-way if/elif over SigningMode with subtly different default arms. Extract a single pure helper mapping (SigningMode, str) -> bytes and reuse it from both sites, or raise on unknown modes. As written this is exactly the duplication the refactor was meant to eliminate.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum's boolean cascade has an implicit fallthrough case and should be a lookup table.
issues.detail: The function enumerates three (is_hex, safe_mode) combinations explicitly and silently lands the fourth on a trailing return CHIP_0002. A 2x2 dict keyed by (is_hex, safe_mode) makes the mapping obvious, audit-friendly, and removes the unstated invariant. Bonus: the request type encodes one logical SigningMode value as two booleans plus a derivation, which is its own complecting.

issues.description: Two different things named signing_mode_enum in the same module, plus verify_signature couples a util to the RPC response type.
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines VerifySignature.signing_mode_enum (property) and a top-level signing_mode_enum(request) function with different signatures. Rename the free function. Separately, verify_signature in util/signing.py returns VerifySignatureResponse, coupling the library to the transport schema; return a plain (bool, optional error) and let the RPC layer wrap it.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring is a stale stub referencing a nonexistent `request` parameter.
issues.detail: The function takes keyword-only signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address, but the docstring reads `:param request:` and `:return:` with no content. For a freshly extracted canonical signing library, either delete the placeholder or write one that matches the signature and states the invariants.

issues.description: Variable hex_message holds non-hex bytes in multiple branches; misleading name carried over from old code.
issues.detail: In sign_message, the UTF8 branch holds utf-8 bytes and the CHIP_0002 branch holds a tree hash, yet the variable is still named hex_message. Since the refactor is already touching this block, rename to message_bytes or message_to_sign to stop lying to the reader.

issues.description: current_p2_puzzle_hash duplicates the same uncurry-or-raise pattern across DID and NFT wallets, with a gratuitous error-string regression.
issues.detail: DIDWallet.current_p2_puzzle_hash and NFTWallet.current_p2_puzzle_hash both uncurry, raise on None, else return p2.get_tree_hash(). Extract a small pure helper taking the uncurried result. Also, did_wallet's error message changed from 'Invalid inner DID puzzle.' to 'Invalid DID inner puzzle.' for no reason, which breaks log/test string matches.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the refactor is directionally correct — consolidating sign/verify out of three wallet classes into chia/wallet/util/signing.py removes real duplication. But it stops short: the mode-to-bytes dispatch is still copy-pasted between sign_message and verify_signature with drift-prone default arms, and the (is_hex, safe_mode) boolean cascade should be a 2x2 table. The new util is coupled to the RPC response type, and the module ships two different things named signing_mode_enum. A stub docstring, a misleading hex_message variable name, and a gratuitous error-string change round out the cleanup list. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — none of it is hard, but ship the refactor with the duplication actually removed.
